page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family configured with a compute-oriented 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem totals 8.0 GB of RAM, or 2.0 GB per vCPU, complemented by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Local storage is bundled as a 150 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Hardware vector capabilities include AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) alongside cryptographic acceleration for AES and SHA algorithms. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-quartile single-core metrics, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2,096.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 2,934.18. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle tier, recorded at 6,660.0 in Geekbench and 9,459.22 in PassMark CPU tests. The memory subsystem sustains 73.06 GB/sec read and 60.22 GB/sec write bandwidth on large uncached blocks.

Performance profiles show lower relative efficiency on storage-bound and highly concurrent operations. Database operations scored 1,916.73 in PassMark tests, and static web serving reached 4.46 GB/sec, placing both in the bottom quartile. LLM inference on medium 7B models is also constrained by memory capacity and lack of hardware accelerators. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-threaded instruction processing, this configuration aligns best with software compilation, text processing, continuous integration build jobs, and lightweight microservices that do not require extensive RAM pools.
description: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, a 32 MB L3 cache, and 150 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Architectural features include AVX-512 and cryptographic vector extensions. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core execution alongside mid-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. Tradeoffs appear in database throughput, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression, which test in lower percentiles. With a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU profile and dedicated compute cores, the server is suitable for code compilation, background processing, and compute-focused microservices.
